name: wfuzz
plain: `wfuzz` replaces the word FUZZ in a request with each entry of a wordlist and shows what comes back. It is like ffuf, written in Python, with strong filtering and the option to fuzz several places at once (FUZZ, FUZ2Z, FUZ3Z...).
The core skill is filtering: hide the common reply (by status code, number of lines, words or characters) so only the interesting ones remain.
when: Guess logins on a lab form.
Find virtual hosts through the Host header.

examples.title: Directory discovery
examples.explain: -c colours the output, -z file,LIST loads the wordlist, --hc 404 hides all replies with status 404.

examples.title: Hide by size of reply
examples.explain: --hh hides replies of 1234 characters; --hl lines, --hw words. Find the size of a wrong guess first.

examples.title: Fuzz a parameter value
examples.explain: range,1-200 makes a list of numbers on the fly.

examples.title: POST login form
examples.explain: -d is the POST body; --hs hides replies that contain the regular expression, here the failure message.

examples.title: Two lists at once
examples.explain: FUZZ takes the first list, FUZ2Z the second; wfuzz tries every combination.

examples.title: With a cookie
examples.explain: -b sends a cookie to reach pages behind a login.

options.plain: Payload definition: file,NAME; range,1-100; list,a-b-c; and others.
Target URL (can also be the last argument).
Add a header; may contain FUZZ.
Save results in a format (raw, json, csv, html...).
Hide responses with this status code, lines, words or characters.
Show only responses with these values.
Hide / show responses whose body matches the regex.
How multiple lists combine: product, zip, chain.
List available payloads, encoders, iterators or printers.
Short help; --help for the full list.

mistakes: Not filtering and drowning in 404 lines: always add --hc 404 or a size filter.
Forgetting to quote a URL with ? or & in the shell.
Using the same number for different keywords: the second list is FUZ2Z, not FUZZ again.
Too many threads on a small server.
Fuzzing a real site without permission.
try: Find a hidden directory on a lab server.
Find the size of a wrong answer and hide it with --hh.
Try two lists on a login form on a lab app.
see_also: ffuf(1), gobuster(1), dirb(1), nikto(1), burpsuite, curl(1), and the wordlists in /usr/share/wordlists.
captured_with: Examples are written to explain a technique; they are not captured output.
